PullRequest.Title: Forward and restore editor group visibility for active panes
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Maximizing an editor group hides the other groups, but their active editors were still told they were visible. That let a delayed integrated-browser alert appear while its browser was hidden.

This PR:
- Forwards grid visibility to active panes, combined with whole-editor-part visibility, including newly shown panes and rebuilt or restored layouts.
- Skips unchanged effective visibility notifications, avoiding redundant lifecycle handlers that can reset a displayed Chat Debug session when logging is disabled.
- Restores inline notebook comparisons once a hidden pane becomes visible with a nonzero layout, so maximizing another group does not leave the diff blank.
- Replays skipped Settings and table-of-contents refreshes once Settings becomes visible, so changes made while another group is maximized appear on restore.
- Adds regression coverage for maximize/restore, overlapping visibility, hidden-group opening, layout reconstruction, duplicate notifications, notebook comparison restoration, and Settings catch-up.

It doesn't change browser dialog handling or add browser-specific maximize logic. Settings search persistence is unchanged: the hidden-state clearing mitigation for #135910 is retained, so reloading while Settings is hidden still drops its search.

Testing: `pnpm run build-fast` and `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` passed. `DISPLAY=:99 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/editor/test/browser/editorGroupsService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/notebook/test/browser/diff/notebookDiffEditor.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/test/browser/*.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/test/common/*.test.ts --reporter dot` passed (242 tests). `pnpm run typecheck-client` passed; `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/browser/settingsEditor2.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/test/browser/settingsEditor2.test.ts` passed; `git diff --check` passed. The three Settings regressions failed before the fix. Earlier follow-up checks passed lint and isolated editor-group/notebook-diff suites. The Linux dev build showed Settings updating from font size 14 to 21 after unmaximizing; reload confirmed the unchanged search-clearing behavior. Earlier Linux browser checks covered delayed alerts during maximize, tab switching, multiple browser tabs, layout rebuilding, and saved-layout restoration. Live Chat Debug and inline notebook diff UI were not manually exercised; Windows/macOS UI was not tested.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/349848

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Static call-flow evidence establishes one additional retained focus listener per completed restore of the same model: show unconditionally calls setModel, its same-model branch skips detach, and listener registration remains unconditional. onWillHide does not clear the model store. Exact interactive slowdown depends on restore count.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Retained focus-listener closures/disposables and repeated CellContextKeyManager listener/observable reconstruction on each cell-focus change.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: After R restores without replacing the notebook model, the widget retains R extra focus listeners. Each subsequent cell-focus change performs O(R) context-manager updates rather than a constant number; memory also grows linearly with R.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increasing CPU/allocation work during notebook cell navigation and retained listener memory over a long-lived editor session.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Hiding and restoring the same inline notebook diff did not call NotebookInlineDiffWidget.show again, so visibility cycles did not grow the widget's focus-listener collection.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each visibility restoration now calls show, which invokes NotebookEditorWidget.setModel with the already-attached model. setModel bypasses _detachModel for that model but still registers another onDidChangeFocus listener in _localStore.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added show call at line 545 runs after every hide/show cycle with an existing inline model. Previously setVisible(true) did not call show or setModel; ordinary visibility restoration therefore did not add these subscriptions.
Findings.Title: Avoid accumulating notebook focus listeners on visibility restores
Findings.Impact: Repeatedly maximize/restore another group while keeping an inline notebook comparison open. Every completed restore adds a listener that survives the next hide, progressively increasing the cost of navigating between notebook cells.
Findings.Evidence: NotebookInlineDiffWidget.show (inlineDiff/notebookInlineDiffWidget.ts:41-55) always awaits widget.setModel. NotebookEditorWidget.setModel (notebookEditorWidget.ts:1176-1230) calls _detachModel only for a different model, but unconditionally adds _list.onDidChangeFocus to _localStore at 1226. _localStore is cleared on detach/dispose, not onWillHide (2039-2050). Each listener calls updateContextKeysOnFocusChange, which invokes CellContextKeyManager.updateForElement (view/cellParts/cellContextKeys.ts:90-125), clearing/recreating cell listeners and an autorun and updating context keys.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep comparison/layout restoration, but avoid re-running same-model setModel merely to show the widget, or register the focus listener only when attaching a model so repeated setModel calls remain subscription-idempotent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Maximize/restore groups, overlap whole-part hiding, open an editor in a hidden group, and reconstruct saved/reused layouts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Grid visibility synchronously reaches EditorGroupView and the active EditorPane. Reconstruction checks visibility once for each restored group before installing the grid. Editor opening still awaits the existing setInput operation; this PR does not add another input resolution.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: G editor groups, with at most one active pane notified per group, not every open tab. Reconstruction performs G visibility checks; unchanged effective states are suppressed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Visibility callbacks execute synchronously on the UI thread. Pane-specific asynchronous effects are not awaited by grid propagation; their behavior is accounted for below.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: EditorPanes retains effective visibility and cached pane instances by descriptor. The new guard removes repeated effective-state notifications; newly activated panes explicitly receive the stored state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced SplitView.setVisible through GridView, EditorGroupView, EditorPanes, pane activation and input-setting paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual group counts and costs depend on pane types. No measured layout timings are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Core forwarding and the reconstruction loop do not independently establish a regression. The notebook restoration consequence is reported separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide/restore integrated browsers, canvas native views and extension webview editors.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Browser visibility changes dispatch native-view visibility asynchronously; browser hiding may wait one animation frame. Screenshot capture is not awaited by grid restoration. Canvas reveal waits for native bounds to apply. Extension webview restoration claims its existing overlay or recreates its content according to retainContextWhenHidden.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send native browser visibility changes to the main-process browser service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one effective transition per affected active browser model, with host/model visibility checks suppressing unchanged state; not one call per page element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Grid maximization did not notify the active browser pane through setVisible. Whole-part and tab visibility already used this service path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous, not awaited by grid visibility propagation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture the native page screenshot and encode the result as a background image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A hide can request a final screenshot; visible models retain the pre-existing approximately one-second screenshot timer. Hidden models fail the visibility guard and stop continuing capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The capture implementation and periodic visible-page capture already existed. Group visibility now reaches the host, adding the transition capture while stopping capture once the group is hidden.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Screenshot promises are not awaited by hide/restore; timers are owned by mutable disposables.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply native browser-model bounds before revealing a canvas.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per visible canvas layout, with sequence checks discarding superseded reveals and a single replaceable scheduled visible-layout callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Canvas layout already measured actual visibility and used the same bounds/reveal path; forwarding visibility also schedules its existing next-frame layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounds application gates canvas reveal, not the grid's synchronous visibility change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose/recreate extension webview content unless retainContextWhenHidden retains it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one release/claim per changed active webview. No per-tab traversal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: WebviewEditor.layout already derived visibility from nonzero dimensions and performed these release/claim transitions during maximize/restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Content readiness can follow overlay claim; native grid layout does not await it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Affected active browser/native/webview panes, normally a small subset of G groups; screenshot cost scales with image size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-model asynchronous IPC and screenshot promises; hide uses an animation-frame callback, not a blocking wait. No new all-tab creation loop or subprocess launch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser models optimistically store visibility; hosts deduplicate it. Existing screenshots are retained for placeholders. Canvas scheduled layout and frame handles are replaceable. Extension webview reuse depends on its existing retainContextWhenHidden option.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for forwarding, native IPC, screenshot scheduling, and existing webview dimension-derived visibility.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native IPC duration, image size and extension webview initialization costs are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: The added browser lifecycle work is bounded and implements actual visibility; capture also stops while hidden. No independently actionable performance regression established here.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a still-open inline notebook comparison after its group or the editor part was hidden.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A pending boolean permits one show after effective visibility and a nonzero saved/current layout. show synchronously lays out the widget, then asynchronously sets options/comparison/model. Worker results gate diff decoration rendering but are not awaited by grid restoration. Later cell navigation synchronously invokes all retained focus listeners.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute notebook-level differences in a web worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Comparison reinitialization clears its version cache and issues a notebook-pair diff; visible-range/content updates are debounced and reuse the result when versions match. The worker client is shared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary setVisible(true) did not call inline show and did not restart comparison initialization; input-setting and inline-mode changes already used this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous; needed for comparison decorations, not for returning from setVisible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send notebook/cell contents to the worker for models not already synchronized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two notebook models on a cold synchronization, with all their cells serialized once; warm restoration reuses URI-keyed synchronized models and sends the diff request rather than full notebook copies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same synchronization was already used by the notebook diff on initial input; this PR does not force warm models to resynchronize.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold worker synchronization precedes worker diff; the notebook inputs are already resolved on the restore path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request text-level worker differences for modified cells with visible code editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per recreated visible modified-cell decorator, not all notebook cells; each decorator uses its existing throttled update path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same decoration machinery ran on initial comparison creation; visibility restoration now reinitializes it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous decoration work; does not block grid restoration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R completed restores of one unchanged notebook model, F subsequent cell-focus changes, notebook cell count N, and visible modified-editor count V. The reported issue adds R retained focus listeners and O(R * F) context-manager work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The pending flag clears before show, avoiding repeated show from consecutive layouts. show is asynchronous and not globally serialized; one active notebook pane normally restores once per effective transition. The retained listeners all execute synchronously for each later focus event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The widget and identical NotebookTextModel are reused, so setModel skips detach. However, the unconditional focus-listener registration is not deduplicated and onWillHide does not clear _localStore. Notebook diff version caching is reset on comparison initialization; worker synchronization remains warm.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: traced the added show call through unconditional same-model setModel, retained _localStore subscriptions and CellContextKeyManager.updateForElement rebindings.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Restore frequency and resulting latency are unmeasured, but listener growth and linear focus-event amplification follow directly from the code.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one materially amplified unbounded-retention/CPU regression at notebookDiffEditor.ts:545. Full-model recreation or per-cell filesystem reads on every restore are not claimed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply configuration/schema/managed-setting changes while Settings is hidden, then restore Settings.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hidden refresh attempts set one pending bit. On becoming visible, Settings synchronously refreshes the TOC and forces the settings-tree refresh. renderTree retains its context-view scheduling logic. The restoration does not rerun configuration resolution, extension enumeration or search requests.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Any number of hidden refresh attempts coalesces into one catch-up per visible interval. Work scales with the current settings/search model and TOC groups; tree rendering remains virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous catch-up on the UI thread per dirty hidden interval, with the pre-existing focused-context-view deferral. No Promise.all fan-out or service request is added by restoration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing settings, search and TOC models are reused. The pending bit clears before refresh, and duplicate visible notifications do not trigger another refresh. Existing search-persistence behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced configuration listeners, updateElementsByKey, renderTree, refresh helpers, createGroupIterator and setEditorVisible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large extension-contributed settings inventories can increase catch-up duration; no measured threshold establishes problematic jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional bounded catch-up replaces skipped rendering and preserves model ownership. No high-confidence independent performance defect found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore other active pane types, including Chat Debug logs and terminals.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visibility dispatch synchronously reaches pane handlers. Chat Debug re-shows its current view using in-memory service events; terminal restoration opens xterm only if unopened and flushes/debounces resizing. No editor input is reopened merely because visibility changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send terminal dimensions through the existing process manager when resize handling runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per affected active terminal, with existing resize debouncing; _open returns immediately for an already-open xterm. No new shell subprocess is spawned by setVisible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Part/tab visibility and layout already used the same resize machinery; grid visibility now reaches setVisible as well.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The resize operation is asynchronous; visibility propagation does not await the process-manager result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Affected active pane count, and E cached Chat Debug events copied/filtered on an actual show. Duplicate effective states are suppressed by EditorPanes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous pane callbacks with asynchronous terminal resizing. Chat Debug subscription replacement is bounded, unlike the notebook listener path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Chat Debug loadEvents reads getEvents from the existing service and replaces eventListener through a mutable disposable; it does not reread session log files on this path. Terminal xterm instances and dimensions are reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the inspected Chat Debug, terminal, merge, notebook, interactive/REPL and chat pane lifecycle handlers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cached log size, terminal rendering cost and contributed pane implementations vary. No timing data are available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence finding: lifecycle work is bounded or replaces existing subscriptions, and redundant notifications are reduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide and restore the Remote Environments editor through group maximization.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: RemotesWidget.setVisible starts refresh without awaiting it; cached displayed rows remain available while discovery marks busy. Hiding cancels the widget refresh and showing starts current discovery. Grid restoration is not blocked by discovery completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read SSH configuration and included configuration files through the SSH service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One config-host enumeration per enabled widget refresh; included paths are tracked within parsing. Host names are deduplicated before resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing visibility handler performed discovery on part/tab show, but group maximize/restore did not reach it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates the SSH discovery branch, not editor-grid progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each unique SSH alias using ssh -G.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: H unique aliases produce H subprocesses per completed discovery, limited to 8 simultaneous resolutions per refresh. Cancellation is checked before queued calls; the shown service does not cache resolutions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical discovery existed on other actual visibility changes; maximization now causes this lifecycle transition too.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: SSH discovery completion waits for the bounded queue; grid visibility does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate WSL distributions using verbose and running-list commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two parallel WSL commands per Windows discovery, not one per distribution; no WSL branch off Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same probes ran on the existing remotes refresh lifecycle, not previously from grid visibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates only WSL discovery results; off the grid restoration critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate tunnel/environment availability via existing services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped tunnel enumeration plus sequential additional configured-name queries, and one environment-list refresh when enabled and authenticated. Not one network request per displayed remote row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These service requests already accompanied remotes visibility refresh, but maximization previously omitted the visibility callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous discovery; existing rows can render before these results return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H deduplicated SSH aliases, configured additional tunnel-name count, enabled provider kinds and number of active Remotes widgets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Four provider branches use Promise.all. SSH resolution has an 8-slot limiter per refresh, not a global limiter; WSL uses two parallel commands, additional tunnel queries are serial. The widget cancels its previous request; cancellation does not terminate an already-issued ssh -G process.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Displayed remotes are retained while refreshing; discovery itself refreshes availability rather than treating displayed rows as authoritative cache hits. SSH resolution has no cache in the traced service; environment refresh requests fresh availability. Authentication/service-side network caching can further reduce downstream work but is not assumed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for visibility reachability, alias deduplication, limiter scope, subprocess counts and asynchronous placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence of Remotes editors alongside maximized groups, configuration sizes, provider network latency and service-side caching are unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Existing explicit refresh-on-visible policy now applies to actual group visibility, with cancellation and a per-refresh SSH limiter. No separate high-confidence defect or behavior-preserving correction established; no generic caching recommendation submitted.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all eight changed files and all diff pages against base 6b1715e2dc1771145c06df1de2b56de67542436a. Submitted one high-confidence finding: inline notebook visibility restores accumulate same-model focus subscriptions and amplify later navigation CPU work. Reviewed layout reconstruction, effective-state deduplication, hidden Settings catch-up and transitive native-view/worker/subprocess/network behavior. Static review only; durations and real-world prevalence remain unmeasured. No concrete old performance-regression fix with sufficient provenance was established for internal fix reporting.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
